transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because things at work have just gotten... out of hand. I'm a transportation inspector, and ever since I got this county safety award a while back, certain people there have been coming after me. 

They keep twisting my inspection reports around, and they've started asking these really pointed budget questions. It's like they're actively trying to make me look crooked or something. I brought it up to my supervisor, and he just brushes it off—he says it's just a normal review process. But I know what I'm seeing. I can tell there is a coordinated effort going on to discredit me, and it's just getting to be a lot to deal with.
Can you tell me more about how you know these people are coordinating against you? Have you noticed any specific behaviors or evidence that confirms this to you?

Well, it's exactly what I was just mentioning. The proof is really in how they're handling my paperwork. Right after I got that county safety award, the whole atmosphere shifted. 

I'll turn in my regular inspection reports, and suddenly they're twisting the details around. And then they come at me with these really pointed budget questions. It's not just standard auditing... they ask them in a way that's clearly trying to trap me or make me look crooked. 

When I take it to my supervisor, he just brushes it off. He tells me it's a normal review process. But I've been doing this job long enough to know what a normal review looks like, and this isn't it. You can just tell when it's a coordinated effort to discredit you, you know? It's all too connected to just be a coincidence.
Have you noticed anyone outside of work, like neighbors, friends, or family members, acting differently toward you or being part of this effort to discredit you?

No, I haven't noticed anything like that. My family and friends... they treat me the exact same as they always have. Nobody in my personal life is acting weird or anything. 

It's really just contained to the office and the people dealing with my inspections. Once I clock out and go home, things are normal. The issue is strictly with the people at work who are messing with my reports.
Have you ever felt like people are trying to harm you or conspire against you in any other areas of your life, even when you're not at work?

No, not at all. It's really just like I was saying a second ago. I don't feel like anyone is out to get me or, you know, trying to physically hurt me when I'm at home or just out running errands. 

It's strictly related to my job and those inspections. Outside of that, everything is just... regular life. I don't have this issue anywhere else.
Have you ever had thoughts that people were trying to harm you or conspire against you when you weren't at work, even if just for a short time?

No, I really haven't. Like I just said, it's... it's strictly a work thing. I don't have any thoughts about people coming after me or conspiring against me when I'm off the clock, not even for a short time. 

Once I leave work, I'm just going about my normal day. The whole problem is just those guys at the office and how they're handling my inspection reports. That's really it.

Have you ever had any experiences or thoughts that you could not quite explain, such as feeling like someone was controlling your thoughts or actions, or that you were receiving special messages from the TV, radio, or other sources?

No, I've never had anything like that happen. I don't feel like anyone is controlling my thoughts or making me do things. And I definitely don't get any kind of secret messages from the TV or the radio. I just watch regular shows or listen to music like anyone else. My thoughts are my own, and the only thing going on is what I told you about the guys at work messing with my inspection reports. That's the only thing that's happening.
Have you ever had any beliefs or ideas that others might find unusual or not based in reality, even if they weren't related to work?

No, I haven't. I don't have any weird beliefs or anything like that. I mean, my life outside of the job is just completely normal. I don't have ideas that people would think are crazy or made up. 

The only thing going on is just... exactly what I've been telling you about the guys at the yard messing with my reports. Other than that, I'm just a regular guy. I don't have any unusual ideas about anything else.
Have you ever had any beliefs or suspicions that weren't related to work that others might not understand or seem strange to them?

I feel like we're kind of going in circles here, doc. But no, I don't. Like I was saying, there's nothing strange going on outside of my job. I don't have any weird suspicions about my neighbors or my friends or... or anything like that. 

Everything else is just normal day-to-day stuff. The only issue I'm dealing with is the guys at the yard and what they're doing to my reports. That's really the only thing.
Have you ever had any strong beliefs or suspicions that turned out not to be true, even though you were absolutely sure they were at the time?

No... no, I haven't. If I believe something, it's because it's the truth. I don't just jump to conclusions or make things up. 

If I'm sure about something, it's because I have proof, you know? Like what's happening at the yard with my inspections, I know I'm not wrong about that because I can see it happening. But as for being absolutely sure about something and then finding out later that it wasn't real? No. That hasn't happened to me. I'm a pretty grounded guy.
Have you ever had a belief that you were absolutely certain was true, but others could not see it or agree with you, even when they had all the facts?

No, I really haven't. I mean, if people look at the facts, they see what I see. It's just common sense. 

Like I said, the only thing people might not get right away is what's happening at the yard, but that's only because the guys are good at hiding it. If someone actually looked at the original reports before they got messed with, they'd agree with me. But other than that situation, no, I don't have beliefs that everyone else disagrees with. If I have the facts, people usually see it the same way I do.
Have you ever had a belief that was very important to you, but others could not understand or accept, even when you explained it clearly?

Look, doc, I... I feel like you're just asking me the same thing again using different words. No, I haven't. 

I don't have any weird beliefs that people can't accept. If I explain something to someone, they usually get it because I just stick to the facts. Aside from the guys messing with my reports at work—which, again, they'd understand if they just looked at the actual paperwork—there's nothing else. I'm just a regular guy. I don't have any secret beliefs that nobody else gets.
